newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ exotic forestry on the increase - Statistics NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ exotic forestry on the increase - Statistics NZ.

text.p: The area in exotic forest plantations in New Zealand has increased over 45 percent in the 10 years to 1995, going to 1.6 million hectares from 1.1 million hectares in 1985, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.

"Land use patterns in 1995 now show 10 percent of total farm land in exotic tree plantations, 81 percent in grazing, arable, fodder crops and fallow land, one percent in horticulture and eight percent in other uses including conservations and native plantings," SNZ said.
It said there was also a significant increase in dairying.

"In the decade ending 1995, there was a 47 percent increase in dairy farm numbers in the South Island with the number of dairy farms going from 1,450 farms in 1985 to 2,134 in 1995. This reflects a change in land use from sheep farming," SNZ said.

By comparison, total North Island dairy farms decreased by one percent over the same period, going from 14,528 to 14,387 dairy farms. SNZ said the decrease was due to a rationalisation toward farm units of larger size rather than any decrease in dairying activity.
